claim: Engineering analyses found the tower's safety margin against falling over was very low, with a factor of safety of only 1.07 to 1.15.
title: Jamiolkowski (2001), The leaning tower of Pisa: End of an Odyssey, ISSMGE conference proceedings
quote: its factor against falling over is very low and falls in the range of 1.07 to 1.15

claim: In the second half of 1993, 600 tonnes of lead weights were placed on the north side of the foundations, on a removable concrete ring cast around the base of the tower.
title: Burland, Jamiolkowski & Viggiani (2009), Leaning Tower of Pisa: behaviour after stabilization operations, ISSMGE Int. J. of Geoengineering Case Histories 1(3)
quote: Temporary stabilisation of the foundation was achieved during the second half of 1993 by the application of 600t of lead weights on the north side of the foundations via a post-tensioned removable concrete ring cast around the base of the Tower at plinth level

claim: The lead counterweight, placed between May 1993 and January 1994, made the tower reverse the direction of its movement for the first time in its history.
title: Jamiolkowski (2001), The leaning tower of Pisa: End of an Odyssey, ISSMGE conference proceedings
quote: The counterweight placed in the period between May 1993 and January 1994, produced a very positive response of the monument, which, for the first time in its history, inverted the direction of the movement

claim: In September 1995, during an unsuccessful attempt to replace the lead weights with temporary ground anchors, the tower's southward movements accelerated, and the lead load was raised to 900 tonnes to control them; this period is called "Black September".
title: Burland, Jamiolkowski & Viggiani (2009), Leaning Tower of Pisa: behaviour after stabilization operations, ISSMGE Int. J. of Geoengineering Case Histories 1(3)
quote: In September 1995 the load was increased to 900t in order to control the accelerating southward movements of the Tower during an unsuccessful attempt to replace the unsightly lead weights with temporary ground anchors. This difficult period during the Committee's activity has been called "Black September"

claim: While part of the ground structure around the south of the base was being removed to build a concrete ring for the anchors, the tower began tilting south at 3 to 4 arc-seconds per day, with serious concern for its stability.
title: Jamiolkowski (2001), The leaning tower of Pisa: End of an Odyssey, ISSMGE conference proceedings
quote: During the first attempt to remove in small segments the South part of the catino to build the prestressed concrete ring for the ten anchors, the Tower started to tilt towards South at a rate of 3" to 4" per day with serious concern for its stability

claim: Before the final stabilisation works, a safeguard of cables was attached to the tower to prevent any unexpected movement; it was never needed and was never put into operation.
title: Jamiolkowski (2001), The leaning tower of Pisa: End of an Odyssey, ISSMGE conference proceedings
quote: before starting the final stabilisation works under the Tower, to prevent any unexpected adverse movement during this intervention, a safeguard structure was implemented consisting in a cable stay ... Providentially, the underexcavation interventions did not require the use of the safeguard structure so that the cable stay was never put into operation

claim: The fix was underexcavation: highly controlled extraction of ground from beneath the north side, which made the north edge settle and reduced the tower's inclination by one tenth of its 1993 maximum.
title: Jamiolkowski (2001), The leaning tower of Pisa: End of an Odyssey, ISSMGE conference proceedings
quote: The method chosen to stabilise the Tower consisted in highly controlled ground extraction, named underexcavation, which by inducing the settlement of the North edge of the plinth, allowed to reduce the inclination of the Tower by 1800 arc-seconds, one tenth of the maximum tilt, recorded in 1993

claim: 38 cubic metres of soil were removed from underneath the raised end of the tower to slightly straighten it by 45 centimetres, returning it to a position last seen in 1838.
title: Imperial College London news (2011): Prof. who helped save Leaning Tower of Pisa
quote: which saw 38 cubic metres of soil removed from underneath the raised end of the tower to slightly straighten it by 45 centimetres, returning the tower to a position previously seen in 1838

claim: In March 1990, Professor John Burland of Imperial College London was asked to join a 14-member committee charged with stabilising the tower.
title: Imperial College London news (2011): Prof. who helped save Leaning Tower of Pisa
quote: In March 1990, Professor Burland was asked to be part of a 14 member committee charged with stabilising the tower
